rubrics.justification: The response substantially contradicts the provided laboratory grading of 4AA by downgrading the embryo to ~3-4BB/3BC and adds uncertain image features (sparse TE, loosely grouped ICM, fragment/extruded body) that are inconsistent with the known case description.
It integrates most relevant patient factors—young age, ovarian reserve, endometriosis, prior outcomes, sperm parameters, BMI, and lining—with embryo prognosis, though some links are overstated.
The structure is logical, but the prognosis is built on an incorrect morphology assessment and includes somewhat arbitrary percentage adjustments, limiting internal validity.

Several recommendations are not strongly guideline-based for this scenario, including routine corticosteroids, ERA after limited failures, broad thrombophilia testing, and a strong push toward PGT-A/freeze-all in a 28-year-old without clearer indication.
The response gives concrete next steps for transfer and future planning, but some actions are not appropriately evidence-based or may be premature for this case.
